provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Civic: obedience
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the importance of obedience.
The pupils should be able to list rules at home and school.

Introduction:
We have learned about good manners in our previous lessons.
Today we will talk about why we must obey rules.

Content:
Obedience means doing what you are told by your parents or teachers.
Rules keep us safe and happy in our homes and schools.
For example, we must not play with fire near the kerosene stove.
At school, we must line up quietly when the bell rings.
When we obey rules, we show respect and avoid punishment.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to make a poster showing rules at home and at school.

Evaluation questions:
Why is obedience important?
Name two rules at home.
What happens when we do not obey rules?

Summary:
Obedience helps us stay safe and show respect to others.

topics.title: Civic: honesty
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what honesty means.
The pupils should be able to tell one story about an honest child.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about obedience.
Today we will talk about being honest in everything we do.

Content:
Honesty means telling the truth and not stealing.
An honest person returns things that do not belong to them.
For example, if you find a lost bag of money in the market, you should give it to the market leader.
When you are honest, people trust you and respect you.
There was a boy named Emeka who found a wallet with money.
He returned it to the owner who gave him a gift for his honesty.

Class activity:
Pupils will role-play a story about being honest in the school compound.

Evaluation questions:
What does honesty mean?
What should you do if you find something that does not belong to you?
Why is honesty important?

Summary:
Honesty helps us build trust and respect among people.

topics.title: Social: cooperation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain the meaning of cooperation.
The pupils should be able to work together in a group task.

Introduction:
We have learned about honesty and obedience.
Today we will talk about how we can work together with others.

Content:
Cooperation means working together to achieve something.
When we cooperate, we help each other and share ideas.
For example, when cleaning the classroom, some pupils can sweep while others arrange chairs.
In a market, traders cooperate to attract customers and make more sales.
When we cooperate, we finish tasks faster and better.

Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups of four to build a tower using blocks.

Evaluation questions:
What is cooperation?
Name two ways we can cooperate at school.
Why is cooperation important?

Summary:
Cooperation helps us achieve more when we work together.

topics.title: Social: religion in our community
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify places of worship.
The pupils should be able to explain why we should respect different religions.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about cooperation.
Today we will talk about religion and how we respect different beliefs in our community.

Content:
People in Nigeria worship in different places like churches, mosques and traditional shrines.
We must respect all places of worship because they are important to different people.
For example, we should be quiet when passing a church during Sunday service.
Peaceful worship means people pray without fighting or causing trouble.
In Nigeria, people of different religions live together in peace and harmony.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw and label different places of worship in their community.

Evaluation questions:
Name two places of worship in Nigeria.
Why should we respect other people's religions?
What does peaceful worship mean?

Summary:
We should respect all religions and worship peacefully in our community.

topics.title: Security: first aid
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list simple first aid steps.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate when to call for help.

Introduction:
We have learned about respecting different religions.
Today we will talk about what to do when someone gets hurt.

Content:
First aid is the help we give to someone who is injured before they see a doctor.
Simple first aid steps include cleaning small wounds with clean water.
If someone is bleeding, we should cover the wound with a clean cloth.
We must call for help when someone is seriously hurt or cannot move.
For example, if a pupil falls from a danfo and cannot stand, we should call an adult immediately.

Class activity:
Pupils will practice how to help an injured friend in the classroom.

Evaluation questions:
What is first aid?
Name two things to do for a small wound.
When should you call for help?

Summary:
First aid helps us care for small injuries before getting professional help.

topics.title: Security: fire safety
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain fire prevention rules.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate stop, drop and roll.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about first aid.
Today we will talk about how to stay safe from fire.

Content:
Fire prevention means keeping away from things that can cause fire.
We must not play with matches or near cooking stoves.
During the harmattan season, we should be extra careful with fire.
If clothes catch fire, we should stop, drop to the ground and roll to put out the fire.
We should also know the emergency number 112 for fire fighters.

Class activity:
Pupils will practice the stop, drop and roll technique in the school compound.

Evaluation questions:
Name two ways to prevent fire.
What should you do if your clothes catch fire?
Who should you call if there is a big fire?

Summary:
Fire safety rules help us prevent fires and know what to do if there is a fire.

topics.title: Civic: leadership
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify leaders in their school.
The pupils should be able to explain what makes a good leader.

Introduction:
We have learned about fire safety.
Today we will talk about leadership and who leads us in school.

Content:
Leaders are people who guide and help others.
In school, leaders include class monitors, head boy, head girl and prefects.
Good leaders listen to others and help solve problems.
For example, a class monitor helps the teacher to keep the classroom quiet.
Good leaders serve others and do not misuse their power.

Class activity:
Pupils will vote for a class leader and explain why they chose that person.

Evaluation questions:
Name two leaders in your school.
What makes a good leader?
How can leaders help in the classroom?

Summary:
Good leaders serve others and help make our school a better place.

topics.title: Social: festivals
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name two Nigerian festivals.
The pupils should be able to describe how people celebrate festivals.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about leadership.
Today we will talk about Nigerian festivals and how we celebrate them.

Content:
Nigeria has many festivals like New Yam Festival, Eid and Christmas.
Festivals are times when people celebrate their culture and religion.
During festivals, people wear new clothes, cook special food and visit friends.
For example, during New Yam Festival, people eat yam dishes and dance to traditional music.
Our festival fair will show different Nigerian cultures through food, music and clothes.

Class activity:
Pupils will prepare a small display about their favorite Nigerian festival.

Evaluation questions:
Name two Nigerian festivals.
How do people celebrate festivals?
What will you show at our festival fair?

Summary:
Festivals help us celebrate our culture and bring people together.

topics.title: Security: emergency numbers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall important emergency numbers.
The pupils should be able to role-play calling for help.

Introduction:
We have learned about Nigerian festivals.
Today we will talk about who to call when there is an emergency.

Introduction:
We have learned about Nigerian festivals.
Today we will talk about who to call when there is an emergency.

Content:
Emergency numbers help us get help quickly when there is danger.
In Nigeria, important numbers include 112 for police, 0800 112 112 for fire and 112 for ambulance.
We should only call these numbers when there is a real emergency.
For example, if there is a fire in the market or someone is very sick.
We should learn these numbers and teach our family members.

Class activity:
Pupils will role-play different emergency situations and practice calling for help.

Evaluation questions:
What is the emergency number for police?
When should you call emergency numbers?
Name one emergency situation where you would call for help.

Summary:
Knowing emergency numbers helps us get help quickly when we need it.

topics.title: Revision and project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to answer questions about values.
The pupils should be able to complete their values chart project.

Introduction:
This week we will revise what we have learned this term.
We will also work on our values chart project.

Content:
We have learned about obedience, honesty, cooperation and many other values.
A values chart shows the important values we should practice in our daily life.
For our project, each pupil will make a chart showing three values and how to practice them.
We will have a values quiz to test what we have learned this term.

Class activity:
Pupils will work on their values chart and participate in a class values quiz.

Evaluation questions:
Name three values we have learned this term.
How can you show honesty at home?
Why is cooperation important?

Summary:
We have learned many important values that help us live well in our community.
